A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure factors of phi29 polymerase have been corrected to remove the lattice-translocation defect and the resulting electron density maps have been improved by a significant margin.
the X-ray intensity correction is a useful tool for the structure determination of protein crystals that contain lattice-translocation defects.
the X-ray diffraction data were collected on a single crystal containing lattice-translocation defect and the crystallographic data were corrected for the lattice-translocation defect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to correct the observed structure factors to obtain the structure of a single lattice in the case of crystals with lattice-translocation defects.

the correction procedure can be applied to any X-ray intensity data set containing lattice-translocation or other defects that cause the observed structure factors to be a weighted sum of structure factors from two or more identical but translated lattices.
the correction method described here can be applied to any crystal with lattice-translocation defects and is not restricted to the specific example of the phi29 DNA polymerise.
